course_name_original: Procedimientos de Evaluación de la Integridad Estructural
prerequisites: Prior completion of a general materials science course at the Bachelor's degree level.

learning_outcomes.text: Ability to evaluate the structural integrity of components subjected to mechanical loads and to predict their useful life in situations of fatigue, stress corrosion cracking, and creep.
Ability to analyze the ultimate causes of component failures that occurred during service, to adopt appropriate corrective measures, and to prevent new failures.
Understand the main existing structural integrity procedures and their limitations of use.
Understand the main techniques for the evaluation of components against fracture/plastic collapse failures.
Understand the main techniques for the evaluation of components against fatigue failures.
Understand the main techniques for the evaluation of components against creep failures.
Understand the main techniques for the evaluation of components against failures due to environmental deterioration phenomena.
Understand techniques for evaluating situations where interaction between several failure modes occurs.
Understand special or advanced analysis techniques (leak before break, dissimilar materials, notch evaluation).
Familiarize with the structure of a structural integrity procedure.
Perform structural integrity assessments following the recommendations of a structural integrity assessment procedure.
Use software for performing structural integrity assessments.
Ability to apply theoretical models and to use physical and mathematical tools for diagnosing and solving problems.
Foster in the student an interest in acquiring practical knowledge.
Lay the foundations so that the student is capable of applying the acquired knowledge in engineering.
Formation of an open, critical, cooperative, and entrepreneurial spirit.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to structural integrity assessment procedures. What is a structural integrity assessment procedure? Structure of a procedure. Main procedures in use for structural integrity.

Structural integrity assessment techniques for fracture/plastic collapse. Failure Assessment Diagram (FAD). Crack Driving Force Diagram (CDFD). Initiation analysis vs. Tearing analysis. Special or advanced analysis options (Leak before break. Dissimilar materials. Notch analysis).
Structural integrity assessment techniques for fatigue. Fatigue of unfissured elements (welded, non-welded). Fatigue of fissured elements.
Structural integrity assessment techniques for creep. Creep of unfissured elements. Creep of fissured elements.

Structural integrity assessment techniques for environmental deterioration. Evaluation of stress corrosion cracking processes. Evaluation of thickness loss due to corrosion. Embrittlement models (hydrogen, neutron irradiation).
assessment_rules: A minimum of 4 points out of 10 is required for the average of the theoretical and practical exams. A minimum of 5 points out of 10 is required for the average of all evaluation activities to pass the course.
